last_transition_reason: The proof establishes exactly the claimed termwise rewriting in Q(q): it expands the q-Pochhammer products, proves (q^(2d);q^(2d))_k = (q^d;q^d)_k (-q^d;q^d)_k for each k, substitutes this into the original summand, and then sums over k=0,...,n-1. No forbidden or undeclared dependencies are used, and the argument matches the lemma and its role in the assembly.
latest_nl_proof:
Fix positive integers d and r with gcd(d,r)=1 and r\le d, and fix n>1 with n\equiv 1\pmod{2d}. These arithmetic hypotheses are not needed for the algebraic rewriting, but they are part of the stated setting.

For each k with 0\le k\le n-1, write
S_k(q):=[3dk+r]_q\,(q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k\,(q^d;q^d)_k^2\,q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2}\big/(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k.
Then by definition,
T_{d,r,n}(q)=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} S_k(q).
Also, the exponent k(d-dk-2r)/2 is an integer by the statement, so the monomial q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2} is a well-defined element of \mathbf Q(q).

Now fix such a k. Using the definition (u;q)_k=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-uq^j), we have
(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1-q^{2d}(q^{2d})^j\bigr)=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1-q^{2d(j+1)}\bigr),
(q^d;q^d)_k=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1-q^d(q^d)^j\bigr)=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1-q^{d(j+1)}\bigr),
and
(-q^d;q^d)_k=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1-(-q^d)(q^d)^j\bigr)=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1+q^{d(j+1)}\bigr).
Therefore
\begin{aligned}
(q^d;q^d)_k(-q^d;q^d)_k
&=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1-q^{d(j+1)}\bigr)\bigl(1+q^{d(j+1)}\bigr)\\
&=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\bigl(1-q^{2d(j+1)}\bigr)\\
&=(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k.
\end{aligned}
This identity is in the polynomial ring \mathbf Q[q], hence also in its fraction field \mathbf Q(q).

Substituting this factorization into S_k(q), we get in \mathbf Q(q)
\begin{aligned}
S_k(q)
&=[3dk+r]_q\,(q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k\,(q^d;q^d)_k^2\,q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2}\Big/\Big((q^d;q^d)_k(-q^d;q^d)_k\Big)\\
&=[3dk+r]_q\,(q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k\,(q^d;q^d)_k\,q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2}\big/(-q^d;q^d)_k\\
&=A_{d,r,n,k}(q).
\end{aligned}
So each summand of T_{d,r,n}(q) is exactly A_{d,r,n,k}(q).

Summing this equality over k=0,1,\dots,n-1 yields
T_{d,r,n}(q)=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}A_{d,r,n,k}(q)
inside \mathbf Q(q).

This is precisely the claimed rewriting, equivalently using
(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k=(q^d;q^d)_k(-q^d;q^d)_k
for each k.

statement_nl: Let [m]_q=(1-q^m)/(1-q). For any parameter u and integer k>=0, let (u;q)_k:=∏_{j=0}^{k-1}(1-u q^j), and let (u,v,w;q)_k:=(u;q)_k(v;q)_k(w;q)_k. Suppose d and r are positive integers with gcd(d,r)=1 and r <= d, and suppose n>1 satisfies n ≡ 1 mod 2d. For 0<=k<=n-1, define A_{d,r,n,k}(q):=[3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2}/(-q^d;q^d)_k, where k(d-dk-2r)/2 is an integer because k(1-k) is even. Define also T_{d,r,n}(q):=∑_{k=0}^{n-1} [3dk+r]_q (q^r,q^r,q^d;q^{2d})_k (q^d;q^d)_k^2 q^{k(d-dk-2r)/2}/(q^{2d};q^{2d})_k. Then in the rational-function field Q(q) one has T_{d,r,n}(q)=∑_{k=0}^{n-1} A_{d,r,n,k}(q). Equivalently, each summand is rewritten using (q^{2d};q^{2d})_k=(q^d;q^d)_k(-q^d;q^d)_k.

domain_restrictions: d and r are positive integers.
n is an integer greater than 1.
k ranges over integers from 0 to n - 1.
The q-Pochhammer symbol (u; q)_k is only defined here for nonnegative integer k.
The factor k(d - dk - 2r)/2 is asserted to be an integer in the stated range of k.
q is treated as an indeterminate in the rational-function field Q(q), not as a specialized numeric value.
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every choice of positive integers d and r with gcd(d, r) = 1 and r <= d, and every integer n > 1 with n congruent to 1 modulo 2d, the finite sum T_{d,r,n}(q) is termwise identical in Q(q) to the finite sum of A_{d,r,n,k}(q) for k from 0 to n - 1, because the denominator (q^{2d}; q^{2d})_k factors as (q^d; q^d)_k times (-q^d; q^d)_k.
quantifier_order: For any parameter u and any nonnegative integer k, define the q-Pochhammer symbols.
For positive integers d and r with gcd(d, r) = 1 and r <= d, and for an integer n > 1 with n congruent to 1 modulo 2d, define the two finite sums.
For each integer k with 0 <= k <= n - 1, define the summand A_{d,r,n,k}(q).
In Q(q), the finite sum T_{d,r,n}(q) equals the sum of the A_{d,r,n,k}(q) terms.
